title: Breast Lift After Pregnancy: When to Have It, When to Wait
meta_description: Have a breast lift once you're done having children and your breasts have settled. Surgeons' advice varies, from at least 3 months after nursing to longer.
excerpt: The right time for a breast lift depends on your life, not your age: done having children, finished breastfeeding, weight stable. Here is how long surgeons suggest waiting, what another pregnancy changes, whether you can nurse afterward and how long a lift lasts.
quick_answer:
When should I get a breast lift after pregnancy?

When you're done having children, your weight is stable and your breasts have stopped changing. ASPS says a later pregnancy can minimize or reverse a lift. After breastfeeding, Shahram Salemy, MD, writing on the ASPS website, suggests waiting up to 6 months; Kristy Hamilton, MD, quoted there, prefers at least 3 months. No source we read sets an ideal age.
